statement: (SGD regime only) With SGD-Nesterov, A1a (airbench96-style, 8.5 full-res epochs) reaches >=75.3% with a thin margin (0.7549, 7.22 s). It sits at a local optimum of zero-cost hyperparameters: augmentation, LS and the LR floor gave no gain >=0.3 pp (E008, E009, E015). Width changes trade badly (E005, E017). The local slope is steep, ~1 pp/epoch. Accuracy slack therefore had to come from a better optimizer or from cheaper epochs, not from retuning SGD. This happened (Muon E019, resolution E006/E021). The 'no retuning' lesson does NOT carry over to Muon (E027: one Muon hyperparameter moved accuracy by 1.18 pp).

Reproducing the futurebiohackers submission's defaults on this machine (fp16 + channels_last, compile max-autotune warmed up in build on synthetic data, GPU-resident uint8 data, GPU-side augmentation) gives a feasible starting point: 3-seed accuracy 0.7549 at 7.22 s.
The futurebiohackers defaults (8.5 epochs, bs 1024, last block 576) give a 3-seed mean accuracy >=0.753 and time <=9.0 s on the A100-SXM4, with complete == True.
Dirac (identity) init of the 3-conv group convs, which the reference recipe apparently lacks, speeds up early optimization. The airbench paper reports it saves about 1.2 epochs on CIFAR-10.
Adding dirac init and cutting epochs from 8.5 to 7.5 keeps 3-seed accuracy >=0.753 and reduces time by >=8% compared with the A1a reproduction.
Capacity in the last group (7x7/3x3 spatial) is cheap in FLOPs. Widening it lets the epoch count fall by more than the added per-epoch cost.
Last block at 768 with 7.5 epochs gives accuracy >=0.753 and time at least 3% below the 8.5-epoch / 576 reproduction.
Brightness/contrast augmentation, a hiverge CIFAR-10 trick, regularizes CIFAR-100 well enough to allow fewer epochs at equal accuracy.

Adding per-batch brightness (+/-0.07 to 0.14) and contrast (+/-0.065 to 0.13) jitter on the GPU at 8.0 epochs keeps 3-seed accuracy >=0.753, while the same 8.0-epoch recipe without it (the run measuring the epoch slope) falls below 0.753.

Per-epoch GPU work drives the score. Tip: E100 (2@16 + 1.25@24 at bs 1536, then 1.25@28 + 2.75@32 at bs 1024, Fable tail with the final window pinned to 8 steps, 32 px Muon lr x1.25, pinned staging) at ~4.46 s. Distinct scored samples are 0.7561 and 0.7516 (mean 0.7538), so it is likely feasible partly by luck (H4). Every measured accuracy/time trade runs at ~0.04-0.065 pp per 1%: the 32 px trim (E089), the 28 px substitution (E090), bs 1024 at 32 px (E084/E095) and bs 1024 everywhere (E104). With ~0-0.05 pp of real margin, schedule and batch reshuffles have converged. The possible exception is the 24 px bridge, which may trade at ~0.13 pp per 1% (H8). Closed time levers: CUDA graphs/launch (E052), Inductor tuning (E066), cuDNN determinism (E036), cudnn.benchmark_limit (E099), prepare (E060, E086), group-2 width cuts (E080), whitening-bias freeze (E093), 32 px trims and the 28 px substitution. Remaining FLOP levers, all to be profiled untimed first: depth cuts (H2.18) and a tile-aligned group-3 width (N2.19). Cost structure: the 32 px phase is ~71% of time and energy-bound; 16 px is low-occupancy.

Progressive resizing makes early epochs much cheaper at little final-accuracy cost, provided the cheap phase uses efficient resolutions (24 px, or 16 px for the first ~2 epochs) rather than 26-28 px. The low-res operator (E016) and final-map geometry (E014) are second-order. Operator: flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then antialiased bilinear downsample, AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1); every shape is compiled and warmed up in build.
A 24->28->32 px schedule, with at most +0.5 epochs to compensate, cuts time by >=5% compared with the best fixed-32 px recipe while keeping accuracy >=0.753.
GELU is more expensive than SiLU or ReLU under compile/fp16, and swapping it costs no accuracy.
Replacing GELU with SiLU at equal epochs reduces time by >=2% and changes 3-seed accuracy by no more than 0.2 pp.

Training only on high-loss examples, as in Selective Backprop / airbench96_faster, cuts backward compute. With 500 images per class and ~8 epochs, the cost of the proxy or forward pass may outweigh the gain.
After 2 full epochs, backpropagating only the top 60% by loss of each batch (losses taken from the main net's own forward pass) reduces time by >=5% with accuracy >=0.753.

(SGD full-res regime) Fixed and per-step CPU/launch overhead (timed prepare, Python/kernel-launch overhead, separate optimizer kernels) is a measurable share of the ~7 s SGD run, and removing it cuts time without touching accuracy.
Compiling the whole train step (forward, backward and a fused optimizer) or capturing it in CUDA graphs removes launch overhead at bs 1024.
A fused/foreach optimizer plus a CUDA-graphed or fully compiled step reduces time by >=2% compared with the reproduction, with accuracy within 0.2 pp.
Prepare (uint8 upload, normalization, whitening init on 5000 images) takes a non-trivial share of timed time and can be shrunk, e.g. fewer whitening images or fused normalization on the GPU.
In the reproduction, prepare is >=3% of prepare+train time. Computing the whitening statistics on 1000-2000 images instead of 5000 cuts prepare by >=30% with accuracy within 0.2 pp.
A larger batch (2000) halves the step count and per-step overhead and raises GPU utilization. LR, wd and momentum need retuning to keep accuracy.
bs 2000 with LR scaled by the kilostep rule, at equal epochs, reduces time by >=3% while keeping accuracy >=0.753.

Accuracy noise sets the usable margin, and decisions near the gate select for luck. Revised noise model: the 3-seed scored mean has a run sd of ~0.2 pp (E101: identical code gave 0.7561 vs 0.7516), and per-seed sd is 0.22-0.38 pp. Rerunning the same seed in a new process moves accuracy about as much as a cross-seed draw does (E028; cuDNN-pick divergence), so pairing by seed barely reduces variance. The SE of a one-process 22-seed off-seed difference is ~0.10-0.11 pp, not the 0.05 claimed in E098. Every off-seed delta since E096 is therefore <1.2 SE: E100 +0.09, E102 0.00, E103 +0.02, E104 +0.12, E105 +0.09. Rules: bit-identical reruns count once. A keep or a close needs >=3 fresh processes per arm on seeds 3-26, or >=2 distinct scored samples plus multi-process off-seed. Support and refutation use the same threshold. The loop broke these rules with E090, E096 and E100, each kept on a favorable first draw. Current tip E100: distinct scored 0.7561/0.7516 (mean 0.7538, n=2), so the local gate is met in ~60% of reruns, partly by luck. No config is robustly feasible yet. E095's support is one off-seed process plus a scored pool that mixes different code. The official 40-seed bar (0.75) is probably cleared by the whole lineage (~0.751-0.753).

For the compiled SGD recipe (A1a), per-seed accuracy is bit-deterministic and run-to-run time variation is small (CV <=0.5%) once compile is warmed up in build. This does NOT hold for the compiled-Muon + progressive-resize tip (E028: per-seed differences of -0.27/+0.19/-0.59 pp on an identical rerun).
Rerunning the identical A1a config gives bit-identical per-seed accuracy and a mean time within 2% of the first run.
Swapping the optimizer (Muon on the conv filters, SGD for biases and head) does not reduce time-to-75% on CIFAR-100, despite its CIFAR-10 gains.
On CIFAR-100, Muon's orthogonalized updates give no sample-efficiency gain over well-tuned high-LR SGD-Nesterov at the airbench96 widths, and the Newton-Schulz steps add per-step cost.
Muon (lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, 3 NS steps) on the conv filters, at the same epochs as the reproduction, gives accuracy no higher than SGD +0.2 pp and time no lower than SGD -2%.

The full-res accuracy-vs-epochs curve near A1a is steep below 8.5 epochs (E007: -0.48 pp for -0.5 ep, ~0.95 pp/epoch, plausibly 0.4-1.5 pp given ~0.25 pp SE) and flatter above 8.5 (reference ablation: 9 ep 75.6% vs 8.5 ep 75.5%). A full-res epoch costs ~0.85 s (~11.8% of time), so cutting full-res epochs costs ~0.08 pp per 1% of time. Every time-saving trade-off must beat this rate.
Unmodified A1a at 8.0 epochs (LR/EMA schedules rescaled to the step count) gives time 6.75-6.85 s and 3-seed accuracy 0.749-0.754, i.e. a loss of <=0.6 pp per 0.5 epoch removed.

Phase-dependent bottleneck. 32 px (cap 94-100% of the time) and 24 px (cap 84%) are energy-bound, so time tracks fwd/bwd energy and memory traffic. 16 px is not at the cap (282 W) but is 98% GPU-busy (E052), so it is bound by low-occupancy kernels and per-step GPU work. Per-step optimizer work costs time at every resolution. It shows up as idle-free GPU work at 16 px (~2 ms per removed step, E038) and as energy at 32 px (E084: +~65 steps at 32 px cost +0.11 s, ~1.7 ms/step). Per-step savings in the 32 px phase (lookahead, renorm, Muon momentum traffic) are therefore live levers. FLOP and byte levers transfer best to the 300 W PCIe judge.

NVML sampling at >=10 Hz during an untimed run of the E026 tip shows board power >=95% of the 400 W cap for >=80% of the 32 px phase. During the 16 px and 24 px phases power stays below 90% of the cap for >=30% of the time, i.e. those phases are launch- or per-step-bound. Observational only; no sleeps or idle gaps added.

Most of E006's -0.69 pp came from the degenerate 2x2 final map at 24 px (24->23->11->5->2, vs 3x3 at 26-32 px); raising the low-res stage to >=26 px recovers most of the loss. (The original random-resized-crop half is retired as moot: E006 never used random-resized crop.)

E006's 9.0-epoch schedule with 26 px instead of 24 px for the first phase, flip + translate-2 at 32 px followed by antialiased downsample (no random-resized crop), gives 3-seed accuracy >=0.752 (>= +0.4 pp over E006) at time <=6.3 s.

With the same 26->28->32 schedule, crop mode (random 26/28 px crops of the flipped/translated 32 px image, no rescaling) gives >=0.3 pp higher 3-seed accuracy than antialiased-resize mode at equal time (+/-1%).

A 9.0-epoch schedule with 26 px for 0-30%, 28 px for 30-60% and 32 px for the last 40% (EfficientTrain++-style long full-res tail), with flip + translate and antialiased downsample, gives 3-seed accuracy >=0.755 and time <=6.7 s (>=7% below A1a's 7.22 s).

In the tip code (E026 lineage), the flip/translate/resize augmentation RNG comes from the trial seed and is reset in prepare. A logged hash of the first batch's augmentation parameters differs across seeds 0-2, and repeating seed 0 reproduces it. E006's 0.02 pp per-seed spread was chance.

Conv FLOPs at 32 px are concentrated in group 2 (~48%: conv1 at 15x15 128->384 plus conv2/3 at 7x7 384->384), then group 3 (~32%) and group 1 (~20%) (estimate from the reference's shapes). Narrowing group 2 is the largest width lever (384->320 cuts ~15% of FLOPs); narrowing group 1 (128->96) saves only ~7%. The reference ablations show capacity is costly to remove on CIFAR-100, so the cut must be paired with the extra epochs it buys.
At 8.5 full-res epochs, group 2 width 384->320 cuts time by >=8% with a 3-seed accuracy loss <=0.4 pp versus A1a, i.e. a better exchange rate than cutting epochs (0.08 pp per 1%).

Zero-time-cost accuracy levers on the current architecture and schedule. Scalar knobs are exhausted: Muon floor, warmup in both directions, head lr 0.4x, head wd, MaxSup, LS 0.2, the bias freeze earlier (E093) and at 20% (E061), lookahead removal (E092), and EMA window/LAWA with BN buffers copied from the net (E081, E083). The one remaining candidate with external support is end-of-run averaging that keeps the BN buffers consistent with the averaged weights (H6.5.4; search 2411.18704: BN, not the parameters, breaks long-window EMA). Phase-local Muon lr is under H10, and filter Muon lr under H7. Retire H6 if H6.5.4 fails.
Budgeted-training results favor LR decaying to zero at the end of a fixed budget. The reference decays only to 0.07x, which leaves end-of-budget gradient noise that hurts final accuracy.
A1a with the LR decaying to 0 at the last step instead of 0.07x (warmup unchanged) raises 3-seed accuracy by >=0.2 pp, with time within +/-1%.

After progressive resizing, BN statistics and the EMA weights are dominated by low-res epochs. Re-estimating BN statistics at 32 px on training data at the end of train (FixRes-style) removes the train/test resolution mismatch cheaply.

On a 24->32 progressive schedule, a forward-only BN re-estimation pass at 32 px over ~10% of an epoch of augmented training data, run inside train, raises 3-seed accuracy by >=0.2 pp at <2% time cost.

Run-to-run noise (~0.2 pp sd on a 3-seed mean; ~0.1 pp per off-seed process), not cross-seed std, is the decision-relevant noise floor. Picking whichever near-threshold variant first clears 0.753 selects for luck. This happened with E026, E046, E068, E090 (distinct mean ~0.7515-0.7524), E096 (bit-identical second scoring; off-seed +0.17 in one process and -0.11 in another, E098) and E100 (0.7561, then 0.7516). Every comparison must pool distinct samples across >=3 processes per arm.

Three neutral perturbations of A1a (a different 5000-image whitening subset, an alternative equivalent autotune choice, an fp16 vs fp32 normalization path) give 3-seed means with std between 0.1 and 0.3 pp.

A1a's mean accuracy over extra seeds 3-10, run through the benchmark's own trial code without editing benchmark/, is >=0.751. That is about 0.4 pp below its seeds 0-2 mean at most, so the baseline is feasible but not comfortably above the 0.75 official bar.

Accuracy at a fixed short budget tracks total training epochs/steps far more than the share spent at 32 px: a 24 px epoch carries most of a 32 px epoch's accuracy value at 57% of its cost. Evidence pattern: E013 put 1.8x more epochs at 32 px than E006 yet gained only +0.26 pp, and E006 (9 ep, mostly low-res) is only 0.22 pp behind 8 full-res epochs (E007) while costing 0.92 s less.
With the E006 operator and no 28 px phase, 6@24 + 4@32 px (10 epochs, ~6.5 s by the cost table) gives >=0.3 pp higher 3-seed accuracy than 4@24 + 5@32 px (9 epochs, ~6.4 s), with time within +2%.

A two-stage 24->32 px schedule (E006 operator, no 28 px phase) at 9.5-10 total epochs, with 24 px for <=60% of steps and LR/EMA rescaled to the step count, gives 3-seed accuracy >=0.753 at time <=6.6 s (>=8.6% below A1a). Predicted time = per-epoch cost table (24 px 0.485 s, 32 px 0.848 s) + ~0.2 s overhead.

16 px epochs are cheap (0.30x of a 32 px epoch at bs 1536, E045). Each early 24->16 swap costs roughly 0.2-0.35 pp, but these are single-run point estimates against references that were often lucky draws (±0.15 pp). The third swap (E046) cost more than the head-on-Muon gain bought: the tip family pools to 0.7533. No further whole-epoch swap is affordable. Giving part of the 24 px bridge back while cutting total epochs (E047) may beat the 3@16 swap at equal time.

A compiled per-epoch cost measurement (2 epochs each, no scored run) shows a 20 px epoch <=0.45x and a 16 px epoch <=0.35x the cost of a 32 px epoch. A 16->24->32 schedule (e.g. 2@16 + 4@24 + 4@32) then reaches >=0.753 at <=6.3 s.

On this energy-bound GPU the optimizer step count is nearly free in time (E010: half the steps, same time), and more updates help accuracy at a fixed epoch budget (E010: bs 2000 cost -0.81 pp). Smaller batches (512-768) should therefore buy accuracy at roughly equal time, unless smaller GEMMs lose efficiency (E012).
A1a at bs 768 (LR/wd/EMA scaled by the same kilostep rule as E010, in reverse), 8.5 epochs, gives a 3-seed accuracy >=0.757 with time within +3% of 7.22 s.

GELU's exact erf costs measurable energy in the fused BN+activation kernels (E003: SiLU saved 2.2%). A cheaper GELU approximation (tanh or polynomial) keeps GELU's accuracy advantage while saving part of that cost, and stacks on any schedule.
Replacing exact GELU with GELU(approximate='tanh') on A1a reduces time by >=1% with a 3-seed accuracy within 0.25 pp of A1a (>=0.7525).

Full-res A1a at 9.0 epochs (LR/EMA rescaled to the step count) gains <=0.3 pp over 8.5 epochs (3-seed accuracy <=0.758) at 7.6-7.7 s, i.e. the slope above 8.5 epochs is less than half the measured 8.0->8.5 slope.

Optimizer quality per update was the binding constraint on CIFAR-100 at ~7-8 epochs, and Muon was the lever: +1.14 pp at equal epochs (E019), a flatter epoch slope (E020), large-batch tolerance (E022, E038). Head on Muon and head lr 0.5x are each worth ~+0.1-0.2 pp on weak evidence. Closed: momentum (flat 0.5-0.6; external work finds momentum schedules cost -1.7 pp on CIFAR-100, search 2603.28921), NS count, cheaper orthogonalizers (MUD/NorMuon are weaker per step and untested on CNNs), head lr/wd. Muon lr on the mixed-batch tip is untested: 32 px x1.25 (E100) and peak 0.28 (E105, base ambiguous) each gave +0.09 pp off-seed in a single process, inside the ~0.1 pp SE. Schedule shape (WSD/cosine vs linear) has never been tested under Muon (N7.4).

Muon momentum and lr sit at a flat local optimum. Momentum is flat in 0.5-0.6 and steep above (E027, E030). LR was flat in 0.20-0.24 on the bs-1024 E026 base (E034). On the mixed-batch tip, a higher lr (E100 32 px x1.25, E105 0.28) moved off-seed by +0.09 pp in one process each, which is noise-level. No lr change is established in either direction.

On the E026 tip, Muon momentum 0.5 (lr 0.24, Nesterov, everything else unchanged) gives a 3-seed accuracy no higher than 0.7574 (tip estimate 0.7554 + 0.2 pp) at equal time. Lowering momentum does not buy usable slack.
On the E026 tip, Muon lr 0.20 (momentum 0.6) gives a 3-seed accuracy >=0.7575 (>= +0.2 pp over the 0.7554 estimate) at equal time (+/-1%).

Muon's remaining overhead is a fixed per-step cost (NS matmuls plus stacking/momentum kernels), ~1.7-2 ms per step at every resolution: idle-free small kernels at 16 px (E038) and energy at 32 px (E084). Renorm cadence saved ~0.08 ms/step (E035). NS 3->2 cost 1.8 pp (E031) and NS 4 bought nothing (E033). External work finds orthogonalizer variants accuracy-equivalent (search: randomized/inexact polar ~= full), so only step count or cheaper per-step traffic can save time. Cheaper orthogonalizers are closed.

On the E026 tip, renormalizing Muon weights every 2 + int(15*progress) steps instead of every step (inside the compiled update, with the step flag passed as a tensor so nothing recompiles) cuts time by >=1.5% with a 3-seed accuracy >=0.7535.

On the E026 tip, 2 Newton-Schulz steps with per-iteration Polar-Express-style coefficients (instead of 3 fixed-coefficient steps) cut time by >=2% with a 3-seed accuracy loss <=0.2 pp against the 0.7554 estimate.

On the compiled-Muon E026 tip, bs 1536 (SGD groups scaled by the kilostep rule, Muon lr/momentum unchanged, LR/EMA/lookahead rescaled to the step count) cuts time by >=3% with a 3-seed accuracy loss <=0.25 pp against the 0.7554 estimate.

Step-indexed schedule reshuffles and trims are no longer a usable lever at the current margin. Low-res reshuffles are exhausted: E070/E071 vs E072/E073 are equivalent at equal time. The 32 px phase is binding: a 0.25-epoch trim (E088/E089) cost ~0.33 pp against its base pool for ~-5% time (~0.065 pp per 1%).

A 4@16 + 4.5@32 px schedule (8.5 total epochs, step-indexed switch, LR/EMA/lookahead rescaled to the step count, E026 operator and compiled Muon) gives a 3-seed accuracy >=0.755 at time <=5.45 s (estimate: 4x0.27 + 4.5x0.85 + Muon/fixed overhead).

An untimed compiled cost measurement (2 epochs each) shows a 12 px epoch >=0.22x and a 20 px epoch 0.40-0.50x the cost of a 32 px epoch. The floor comes from Muon's fixed per-step cost and from small-kernel inefficiency, so replacing a 16 px epoch with 12 px saves <1.5% of total time and is not worth pursuing.

The tip's run-to-run nondeterminism comes from per-process cuDNN algorithm picks (cudnn.benchmark), not from Muon max-autotune. E036 (deterministic cuDNN plus default-mode Muon) gave a bit-identical seed-0 rerun. E042 (default-mode Muon only) stayed nondeterministic (0.7522/0.7549/0.7530). Pinning cuDNN costs ~9.8% time (E036), so determinism is not usable in scored runs. It is a measurement convenience, not a score lever. AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1)'s atomic backward is an unlikely co-source: with a 1x1 output, each gradient goes to a single argmax and nothing collides.

With the Muon update compiled without max-autotune (mode='default') and cuDNN algorithm selection pinned (cudnn.benchmark=False or deterministic algorithms for the 16/24/32 px shapes), two identical runs of the tip give bit-identical per-seed accuracies, with time within +1.5% of 5.50 s.
LS 0.3 was found optimal under SGD (E009, futurebiohackers sweep). Muon fits faster and tuned public Muon recipes use LS 0.09, so the tip may be over-regularized.
On the E026 tip, label smoothing 0.2 instead of 0.3 gives a 3-seed accuracy >=0.7575 (>= +0.2 pp over the 0.7554 estimate) at equal time.

Per-phase batch size. Large early batches hurt (E043: bs 2048 at 16/24 px, -0.49 pp, warmup-confounded). Smaller batches in the 32 px phase help: bs 1024 there gave +0.12-0.18 pp scored and +0.10-0.11 pp off-seed (E084/E085/E095, each one off-seed process) at +2.5% time. E095 pinned the EMA window and kept the gain, so the effect is update count, not window length. bs 1024 everywhere (E104, one process) bought a similar amount per added step, so the rate is ~0.04-0.065 pp per 1% wherever the steps go. That only matches what trims cost and cannot fund a net cut. Porting the window pin to E090 (E096) gave +0.17 off-seed in one process and -0.11 in another (E098), so it is unresolved.

On the tip lineage, use bs 2048 for the 2@16 + 2@24 epochs and bs 1024 for the 4@32 epochs. LR warmup/decay, EMA, lookahead and renorm are indexed by samples seen, and the SGD groups are scaled per phase by the kilostep rule (Muon lr/momentum unchanged). All batch/resolution shapes are compiled and warmed up in build. Prediction: time <=5.26 s (within +1% of E038) and 3-seed accuracy >=0.755. If time is >=5.35 s, the per-step-bound explanation of E038 is wrong.

On the E046 tip (bs 1536), raise only the 16/24 px phases to bs 3072, except the first 0.5 epoch, which stays at bs 1536. The 32 px tail stays at bs 1536. Keep the LR warmup fixed in steps (not samples), so the E043 warmup confound is removed. Decay, EMA and lookahead are indexed by samples. Prediction: time <=4.85 s (>=2% below E046) with a two-run accuracy >=0.7535. Low priority: run only after H8.1.1 indicates whether early batch size, not warmup steps, drove E043's loss.

Only the 16 px phase is launch- or per-step-bound (E045: 282 W, util 82%, ~0.8 s of the tip's time). Capturing the whole train step (fwd, bwd, SGD foreach, compiled Muon, lookahead) in a CUDA graph for the 16 px shape alone removes idle gaps there. The ceiling is ~0.14 s (~3%), with a realistic gain of 1-2%. Graphing 24/32 px gains nothing because those phases sit at the power cap. Fable shows per-resolution whole-step graphs are feasible but publishes no isolated gain, and its 7.6% came mostly from resizing. The gain is per-step, so it transfers poorly to the 300 W PCIe judge.

On the E046 tip (after static shapes, N1a, if that is banked), CUDA-graph the full train step for the 16 px shape only. Capture and warm it up in build on synthetic data, with static input buffers, the LR as 0-d tensors, and a renorm on/off graph-key variant. Prediction: time drops by >=1% (<=4.905 s on E046, or 1% below the N1a tip) with a two-run accuracy >=0.7535. Gate: run only if H2.4.2 shows wall time >=1.3x GPU-busy time at 16 px.

Untimed CUDA-event and profiler timing of the E046 tip per phase. Per step, wall time exceeds GPU-busy time by >=30% at 16 px, and by <10% at both 24 px and 32 px (E045: 24 px is at the cap 84% of the time). Observational only. This gates H2.12.1 and N2c.

The LR warmup was rescaled from ~408 SGD steps to ~256 steps (bs 1536). Halving it (E051, 0.7528) is -0.05 pp against the pooled 0.7533, which is noise, so neither direction is established. The post-mortem mechanism ('warmup protects the 64x-LR SGD biases') has no supporting effect.

On the E038 tip, halving the LR warmup length (in steps; everything else unchanged) gives a 3-seed accuracy >=0.7562 (>= +0.2 pp over the 0.7542 two-run mean) at equal time. If both halving and doubling stay within +/-0.15 pp, warmup is closed.

End-of-run schedule under Muon. The tail (floor-hold at ~96% of steps, lookahead stop, final 8-step EMA at 0.3 lerp every 4, eval on EMA weights with BN buffers from the net) costs no time and is kept. Its mean gain was never shown, though: the evidence is E068 (one high draw) and E069, and no tail vs no-tail off-seed A/B was ever run. Longer windows lost off-seed (E081 -0.09, ~1 SE; E083 LAWA -0.29, ~2 SE). Two explanations compete: (a) averaging higher-LR pre-floor iterates hurts; (b) the averaged weights mismatch the BN buffers copied from the net. External work (2411.18704) directly supports (b). Only H6.5.4 separates them.

On the E056 base, change the Muon-group LR floor from 0.07x to 0.05x and nothing else. Prediction: a two-run pooled accuracy >=0.7548 (+0.15 pp over the pooled 0.7533) at equal time (±0.5%). A result within ±0.15 pp closes it.

Muon flattened the epoch slope, so a group-2 width cut might trade like a schedule trim. E050 (384->352) saved only half its FLOP-proportional time. NVIDIA's tile-quantization guidance explains this: 352 rounds up to 3x128-wide N-tiles, the same work as 384, and 320 does too on 128-wide tiles. Only tile-aligned widths (256, or 320 if cuDNN picks 64-wide tiles) can save FLOP-proportional time. A cut to 256 is a large capacity loss (E017: 320 cost 0.94 pp under SGD), so the prior for a profitable width cut stays low. Decide with existing profile data and a per-layer profile, never with a scored run first.

On the E038 tip, narrow group 2 from 384 to 352 channels (recompiled and warmed up in build). Prediction: time drops >=3.5% with a 3-seed accuracy loss <=0.2 pp vs 0.7542, i.e. <=0.06 pp per 1%, beating bs 1536's 0.064.

Untimed side check: the E038 tip code run through the benchmark's trial code on seeds 3-10 has a mean >=0.7530 and lies within 0.15 pp of its seeds 0-2 two-run mean (0.7542). Then the official 40-seed mean clears 0.75 with >=0.25 pp to spare.

Unbundled determinism probe on the E038 tip: compile the Muon update with mode='default', keep cudnn.benchmark=True, and change nothing else. An untimed seed-0 repeat in a fresh process is bit-identical to the scored seed 0, and time is within +1% of 5.216 s. A real whitening-bias freeze is a FLOP/byte time lever. Detach the bias in forward (Fable e1 and hiverge: F.conv2d(x, w, b if grad else b.detach())), or set requires_grad=False (airbench: 'disable their gradient to increase backward-pass throughput ... without reducing accuracy'). The stem output then needs no grad, so autograd skips group-1 conv1's dgrad (~1.9% of conv FLOPs, low tensor-core efficiency), the stem GELU backward and the bias reduction. Estimated saving ~1-2.5%. As a FLOP lever it should transfer to the 300 W judge. The reference recipes train the bias for only 0.2 epoch (~7 steps at bs 1536, ~3% of steps), with its LR decaying to 0 over that window, then detach. E061 (LR=0 at 20% of steps, -0.08 pp, noise) covers accuracy only for the 20%-of-steps freeze point, and it saved no time.

Confirm in the compiled backward graph that group-1 conv1's dgrad and the stem backward are gone. Prediction: two scored runs average >=1.0% below the base's pooled time (outside the ±0.6% noise band), with accuracy within 0.1 pp of the base on the off-seed seeds 3-10 check. If the time drop is <0.4%, the dgrad is not skipped or is negligible, and H2.15 is refuted as a time lever. Move to an earlier freeze (~0.2 epoch) only after the saving is verified.

Fused BN/GELU/elementwise Triton kernels take 29-31% of GPU time at 24/32 px (E067), but the cost is spread over ~211 kernels per step; the top kernel takes ~0.43 ms/step. Inductor tuning flags are near-optimal and blow the build budget (E066). Torch 2.4 has no fused normalization-backward codegen (that arrived ~2.11), so BN backward likely reads dy and x in separate reduction and dX passes. The only lever left is a hand-written Triton fused BN(+GELU) backward for the dominant 32 px layers. It is math-equivalent and saves energy-proportional bytes, but it costs high effort and has a bounded gain. A bias-only BN (frozen weight), as in Fable/hiverge, saves essentially no backward compute, because dX needs both per-channel reductions anyway.

At ~7-8 epochs and ~240 steps, the remaining accuracy deficit is set by structural properties of training, not by scalar hyperparameters. Implication: rank new accuracy candidates by expected structural effect (>=0.15 pp) and stop generating scalar-knob variants.

The Muon filters feed BN, so the effective relative update size is (Muon step)/||w||, and the renorm target norm acts as a second, implicit LR schedule. hiverge and Fable decay the renorm target linearly from 0.5012 to 0.0786 over the run. Combined with the LR decay to 0.05x, that keeps the relative step from collapsing late (it ends at ~0.3x instead of 0.05x of its start value). The tip adopted hiverge's renorm cadence (E035), but the tree has never examined its target-norm schedule. If the tip renorms to a constant norm, its late relative step is much smaller than in the CIFAR-10 SOTA recipes. This is a change of schedule shape across the whole run, not the end-only floor change that E057 found null.

If the off-seed loss is >=0.15 pp, lookahead is carrying real smoothing on the ~240-step schedule, and the line closes.

Calibrate the off-seed instrument before more off-seed verdicts. Run the unchanged tip on seeds 3-10 in fresh processes until there are >=2 non-bit-identical samples, which samples the training-divergence mode. Prediction: the sd of the 8-seed off-seed mean across non-identical reruns is 0.07-0.15 pp, so a paired A/B difference has SE ~0.1-0.2 pp, and each of E077/E078/E079/E081/E084's off-seed deltas is <1.5 SE. If the sd is <0.05 pp, the instrument is sharp and the past off-seed verdicts stand.

Accuracy at the tip is bounded by late training at test resolution (32 px samples x updates in the final phase), not by total steps or epochs. The evidence is weak. The 32 px trim (E088/E089 pool 0.7522) and the equal-step 28 px substitution (E090, ~0.7515-0.7524) are equal within ~0.01 pp, which cannot separate 'exposure binds' from 'total updates matter'. E104 leans toward placement-independence. E102 (stem bias trained into the 32 px phase) was null. The direct discriminating test against the rival view, that the 24 px bridge is worth more per second (H8), is N8.2.1.

Resolution-statistics adaptation. The antialiased downsample changes patch statistics, so each resolution switch shifts the stem-output distribution. The 64x-LR whitening bias and the BN affine parameters absorb that shift. Freezing the bias before the later switches removes this adaptation. Evidence: E093 (freezing at 0.2 epoch cost -0.44 pp off-seed and -0.5 pp scored, the largest clearly real recent effect). The current freeze sits at ~41% of samples, inside the 24 px phase, before the 28 and 32 px switches.

Move the whitening-bias freeze from ~41% to ~70% of samples, with never-freeze as a second arm. Prediction: the best arm gains >= +0.1 pp off-seed. Outcome E102 (70% arm only): off-seed 0.00 vs tip (one process), scored 0.7521, time +1.2%. The never-freeze arm was skipped, so the pre-registered closure condition (both arms within ±0.05) was not met.
Placement of updates: added steps at low resolution buy little or nothing, while added steps at 32 px buy ~0.1-0.18 pp (E084/E095). This is the direct rival of H10.1's placement-independence.

Same run as H10.1.1, opposite prediction: an off-seed gain <= +0.03 pp from ~53 added low-res steps; a gain >= +0.08 refutes it. Outcome E104: +0.12 off-seed (one process, SE ~0.1), scored -0.13 pp vs the tip pool. Leans toward refutation, but this needs a multi-process replicate.

The bs-1024 32 px gain is a Muon path-length effect, not an update-count effect. Muon's orthogonalized update has a size set by the lr (and the shape scale), not by the gradient. At a fixed sample-indexed lr, 1.5x more steps at 32 px means ~1.5x more total filter movement (relative to ||w||, since the filters are renormed). If so, a larger Muon lr in the 32 px phase alone should reproduce the gain at zero time cost. The SGD-era adaptive-batch literature increases the batch late (search), so a late small-batch gain fits a Muon-specific mechanism better than a generic noise one.

Raise the conv-filter Muon lr by x1.25 in the 32 px phase only (run on the E090 base, a deviation from the E086 spec). Prediction: off-seed >= +0.08 pp at equal time. Outcome E100/E101: off-seed +0.09 paired vs the E096 baseline (one process; corrected SE ~0.1), scored 0.7561 and 0.7516 (distinct mean 0.7538). E105 (global 0.28, base ambiguous) gave the same +0.09. Not established. Re-decide in N4.tip with >=3 processes per arm, and add a matched global-lr arm on E090 to separate phase-local path length from 'just a higher lr'.

Extend the bs-1024 tail to bs 768 in the 28/32 px phases (E100 base; samples-indexed; SGD by the kilostep rule; Muon unchanged; window pinned to 8 steps; static shapes warmed in build). Pre-registered time: +3-4.5%. Prediction: off-seed gain >= +0.25 pp over >=3 processes per arm, i.e. above 0.065 pp per 1%. A gain <= +0.12 pp closes the per-phase batch line. Low prior: E104 shows added steps buy ~0.04 pp per 1% anywhere. bs 768 at 32 px also gives M = 6912 = 54 tiles of 128, i.e. 2.5 waves on 108 SMs (search: NVIDIA wave quantization), so per-step efficiency drops.

In build, set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark_limit=0 so cuDNN v8 tries every available conv algorithm for each static train shape (16/24/28/32 px, bs 1536/1024) and the eval path, instead of the default 10. Change nothing else, and check that build stays under 600 s. Log per-phase epoch times and per-(layer, shape) conv kernel names against the E090 defaults, which also feeds H4.5.1. Prediction: at least one 24/28/32 px shape picks a different kernel, and mean total time falls by >=0.8% over two scored runs. Accuracy is math-equivalent within noise (distinct pool within 0.1 pp of the E090 family). If the kernel names are identical to the default picks, or time changes by <0.3%, the lever is closed.

Depth cuts as a time lever. Width cuts failed because of tile quantization (E080). Removing a conv removes whole cuDNN kernels and ~23 elementwise kernels, so the saving should be close to proportional. In airbench96 each group is conv1 -> pool -> BN -> GELU, followed by a residual branch conv2 -> BN -> GELU -> conv3 -> BN added to the post-pool x0 (search: airbench96.py). So a depth cut must be defined as a 1-conv residual branch or as dropping the branch. Approximate conv MACs per image at 32 px: g1 conv1 27M, conv2/3 33M each; g2 conv1 100M, conv2/3 65M each; g3 conv1 98M, conv2/3 27M each. Group 2's conv3 is the largest single cut (~14%); g1 conv3 (~7%) touches the largest activation traffic (31x31x128), and g3 conv3 (~6%). External prior is weak: airbench95 (2 convs, no residual) does about half the per-epoch FLOPs, but no isolated ablation exists. Capacity is valuable on CIFAR-100 (E017, E050).

Untimed first. On the E100 net, profile per-step time and NVML energy at 32 px and 28 px (bs 1024) and at 24 px (bs 1536) for three variants, each reducing one group's residual branch to a single conv plus the skip: (a) group 2 (~14% of conv MACs), (b) group 1 (largest elementwise traffic), (c) group 3. Prediction: at least one variant cuts projected total run time by >=6% over the E100 schedule. Score only that variant, with the 32 px phase lengthened to spend half the saving (net ~-3%). Decide on >=3 off-seed processes per arm, within 0.05 pp of E100. If no variant saves >=6%, close depth cuts without a scored run.

The judge is a 300 W A100 PCIe; local runs are on a 400 W SXM4. Untimed analysis of existing NVML logs (E045 and later), with no power-limit changes: project each candidate's judge time as the sum over phases of max(phase energy / 300 W, phase GPU-busy time). Prediction: the E090-vs-E095 time gap widens by >=1.1x on the projected PCIe times, because the 32 px work that E090 swaps for 28 px is energy-bound. Per-step levers (bs 1024 at 32 px) cost relatively more there. Use the projection only to break ties between configs whose measured local times are within 3%.

Extended off-seed instrument and tip decision. Run the unchanged E090 config and the E095 config on seeds 3-26. Prediction: E090's mean is <=0.7530 and E095's is >=0.7540. Outcome: E098 confirmed E090 at 0.7525, but it ran E096 instead of E095, in one process per arm. The claim that E095 is the robust fallback has never been measured. Superseded by N4.tip (>=3 processes per arm).

Re-decide the tip lineage with the corrected instrument. Free step first: compute the within-seed cross-process sd from the existing E028/E094/E098 per-seed logs and checksums. Then, untimed through the benchmark's trial code, run E090, E096 (window pin), E100 (window pin + 32 px Muon lr x1.25) and E095 (bs 1024 at 32 px on the 4@32 schedule) on seeds 3-26, in >=3 fresh processes each. Predictions: (1) within-seed cross-process sd >=0.2 pp, so seed pairing reduces variance by <30%; (2) pooled E100 - E090 < +0.1 pp, i.e. the +0.09 single-process estimates were noise; (3) pooled E095 - E090 >= +0.08 pp, i.e. the bs-1024 32 px gain is the one replicated lever. If E100 - E090 >= +0.1 pp with SE <=0.06, E100 is banked and H10.2 gains support. If E095 is not >= +0.08, no config is robustly feasible and accuracy must be found before any further cut.

The 24 px bridge buys accuracy at about twice the rate of the 32 px phase. E064/E065 vs E062/E063: +0.12 pp for +0.9% time (~0.13 pp per 1%). E070's trim: -0.25 pp for -1.8% (~0.14 pp per 1%, against a lucky pool). The 32 px trim (E088/E089) cost ~0.065 pp per 1%. If this holds, moving time from the 32 px phase into the bridge at equal total time adds accuracy. H11 (late full-res binds) predicts the opposite, so this is the direct discriminating test.

On E100 code, run 2@16 + 1.75@24 (bs 1536) + 1.25@28 + 2.5@32 (bs 1024): +0.5 epoch at 24 px funded by -0.25 epoch at 32 px. Switches, LR, floor-hold and tail are indexed by samples; the window stays pinned to the last 8 steps; all shapes are already warmed in build. Pre-registered time: within ±1% of E100 (0.5 x ~0.52 s vs 0.25 x ~0.9 s plus step-count change). Prediction (H8): pooled off-seed gain on seeds 3-26 >= +0.1 pp over >=3 processes per arm, and two distinct scored samples not below E100's distinct mean. If the gain is <= -0.05 pp, H11's late-full-res claim beats the bridge-value claim and N8.2 is refuted.

Under Muon, per-batch data composition and augmentation, not scalar optimizer knobs, are the remaining zero-time accuracy sources. Every augmentation test (E008 brightness/contrast, E016 crop vs resize) ran under SGD, and the loss and regularization tests were scalar. Muon fits ~1.1 pp better and the tail adds averaging, so the balance between regularization and gradient variance has moved. Fort et al. 2021 (search) report that augmentation variance, not just the augmentation, harms generalization on CIFAR-100. To fund another ~5% cut, a lever must show >= +0.15 pp pooled over >=3 off-seed processes at unchanged time.

Multi-sample augmentation at equal compute. Drawing 2+ augmented copies of the same image within a minibatch, with batch size and step count fixed, lowers test error, and on CIFAR-100 the benefit saturates near 4 copies. The optimal LR is unchanged at large batch. Risk at ~7 epochs: unique-image coverage in the affected phase is halved.

On E100, in the 32 px phase only (bs 1024), build each batch from 512 unique images x 2 independent augmentation draws. Translate offsets are drawn independently per copy; the alternating-flip copy keeps its scheme and the second copy gets the opposite flip. Samples per step, step count and shapes are unchanged, so time stays within ±0.5%. The 32 px phase then covers ~1.4 unique epochs instead of 2.75. Prediction: pooled off-seed gain on seeds 3-26 >= +0.1 pp over >=3 processes per arm. If it is <= -0.15 pp, data coverage dominates at this budget and the line closes.

Class-balanced minibatches. With ~10-15 images per class per batch over 100 classes, a uniform permutation leaves per-class counts per batch highly variable. Stratified batches reduce gradient variance from class imbalance at zero compute, which may matter in a ~280-step run.

On E100, replace each epoch's uniform permutation with a stratified one: every batch holds floor or ceil of bs/100 images per class in random order, generated on the GPU from the trial seed inside train, so no data touches import or build. Samples, steps and shapes are unchanged; time within ±0.3%. Prediction: pooled off-seed gain on seeds 3-26 >= +0.1 pp over >=3 processes per arm. A result within ±0.05 pp closes it.

Augmentation strength under Muon. Translate magnitude was never tuned, and late-phase regularization was never tested under Muon. Muon's faster fitting may now leave room for stronger geometric augmentation in the final full-resolution phase, even though under SGD more augmentation did not help (E008).

On E100, raise translate from 2 to 4 px (reflect padding, same fused GPU op) in the 28/32 px phases only, leaving the low-res phases unchanged. Time within ±0.5%. Prediction: pooled off-seed gain >= +0.1 pp over >=3 processes per arm. If it is <= -0.1 pp, the short budget is under-fitting under Muon too, and augmentation strength is closed.

Group-3 width set by tile alignment. Convs run as implicit GEMMs. Group 3's 576 channels = 4.5 x 128, so with 128-wide N tiles every group-3 GEMM (fwd N=K, dgrad N=C, wgrad M=C*9) already pays for 640. Widening to 640 would then add capacity at near-zero conv time (only ~11% more group-3 elementwise work at small 7x7/3x3 maps), while 512 could save more than its FLOP share. This is consistent with E080 (352/320 recovered only 33-60%).

Free first: read the logged cuDNN/cutlass kernel names for the group-3 convs at 28/32 px (E094/E099 logs). If they use 64-wide N tiles, close without runs (576 = 9x64 wastes nothing). Otherwise, untimed profile of group-3 widths 512/576/640 on E100 (all shapes warmed). Prediction: 640 adds <=1.5% total time and 512 saves >=3%. If 640 is near-free, score it on E100. Prediction: pooled off-seed gain >= +0.1 pp over >=3 processes per arm, which beats the 0.065 pp per 1% bar, and the extra margin could fund a 32 px trim.

Muon lr schedule shape. Only the floor and the warmup endpoints were tuned under Muon; the linear-decay shape was inherited from SGD. A warmup-stable-decay shape keeps a high relative step longer and decays more steeply before the floor-hold, which may suit Muon's fixed-size updates in a ~280-step run. Low prior: E081/E083 show iterates from higher-LR phases hurt averaging, and every scalar schedule knob so far was null.

On E100, Muon groups only: hold the peak lr until 50% of samples, then decay linearly to the existing floor at the existing floor-hold point (~96%). Warmup, SGD groups and the tail are unchanged; the lr is set via the existing 0-d tensors, so nothing recompiles. Prediction: pooled off-seed gain >= +0.15 pp over >=3 processes per arm at equal time. A result within ±0.05 pp closes schedule shape.
